preamble: After a nasal, the voiced dental fricative /ð/ can assimilate completely in manner to the preceding consonant, surfacing as a (dental) nasal. In rapid colloquial English, word-initial /ð/ of function words after /n/ regularly becomes [n̪], giving a long nasal that may be the only cue distinguishing 'run the mile' from 'run a mile'. Outside such connected-speech assimilation the change is rare.

examples.note: Connected-speech assimilation after /n/; the alveolar nasal becomes dental and /ð/ becomes a dental nasal.
Same assimilation; the resulting long [n̪n̪] distinguishes 'run the mile' [ˈɹʌn̪ n̪ə ˈmaɪl] from 'run a mile' [ˈɹʌn ə ˈmaɪl].
